survey: Open wooden treasure chest on sand, seen from the front, slightly above and to the left. The box body is a rectangular wooden crate with gold corner posts, a gold top rim and small gold feet. All four feet rest on the sand. A gold keyhole plate is mounted in the centre of the front face. The domed lid is hinged along the back edge and swung up and back. Its front band, with the central hasp tab, is now the raised edge. The underside shows in shadow between the lid and the coins. The right end panel, gold rim around wooden planks, faces the camera at an angle. The lid stays connected to the back of the box with no gap, and it is open far enough to show the contents. Inside, a heap of gold coins rises above the rim, with a blue gem and a pink gem sitting in the pile. In front, one coin leans upright against the front-right foot (E8, ratio 0.79, which fits a tilted disc). A second coin lies flat on the sand, next to a seashell. The pile coins are thin discs seen at an angle, with ratios 0.48 to 0.64 and less than 2.5% off a true ellipse, so they are round. E1 and E6 are bubbles, not parts of the chest. No hinge hardware is drawn, which is an acceptable simplification. Every part rests on or attaches to something, and the chest could open, close and hold its contents.
